overview: This study note explores the practical application of Romans 12, focusing on dedication through the concept of the body, mind, and will as sacrifices. It further details the necessary relationships a Christian must have with other believers and with enemies.

topics.title: Four Therefores in Romans
topics.summary: Romans 12 has four 'therefore' statements that establish a chain of theological progression, starting from the condemnation of the world, moving to justification, assurance, and finally dedication.
key_points: Romans 3:20 is the 'therefore' of condemnation: the whole world is guilty before God.
Romans 12:1 is the 'therefore' of dedication, which serves as the basis for other relationships discussed.

topics.title: Body as Living Sacrifice
topics.summary: The body is a living sacrifice that is given to God, exemplified by the sacrifices of Isaac and Jesus Christ.
key_points: Your body is a living sacrifice to give to God.
Isaac would have died in obedience to God, yielding to God’s will.
Jesus Christ actually died in sacrifice.

topics.title: Mind as Sacrifice
topics.summary: The mind is a sacrifice to God because the Holy Spirit changes your mind by releasing internal power, leading to transformation rather than conformity.
key_points: The world wants to change your mind with external pressure; the Holy Spirit changes your mind by releasing power within.
If the world is in control, you are a conformer; if God controls your thinking, you are a transformer.
Meditating on God’s Word and memorization makes you more spiritual.

topics.title: Will as Sacrifice
topics.summary: The will is a sacrifice to God, and surrendering our will to God allows His power to take over, which provides willpower.
key_points: Your mind controls your body, and your will controls your mind.
Yielding our will to God lets His power takeover, giving us willpower.
Pray about everything and yield the plans of the day to Him.

topics.title: Relationships with Believers
topics.summary: This section covers honest evaluation of spiritual gifts and ministry, faithful cooperation with others, and loving participation in the spiritual body.
key_points: Each Christian must identify the spiritual gifts and ministry one is called to, ideally in a local church.
Be honest in evaluation, as both under and over-evaluating oneself are examples of pride.
Work with others even if you don't like them; no one gift is better or greater than others; gifts are tools to build with.
Love must be honest, not hypocritical, humble, and not proud.
Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, and faithful in prayer, and share the burdens of others.
